answer: Recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments bind an agent's history to a succinct proof, while verifiable delay primitives enforce a fixed computational cost on each new identity, making cloning exponentially costly. Information-theoretically, the entropy of the commitment scheme prevents forgery, so any attempted spoofing requires solving a hard problem analogous to cracking a quill pigment that cannot be replicated; the resulting security margin guarantees Sybil resistance akin to a sonnet’s immutable rhyme scheme.
